chunks: And from him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from 'Abdullah ibn Aban, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the spending upon the dependants, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'What is between the two (limits of) abhorrence – the extravagance and the miserliness'.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended level of spending on family according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) delineates the ethical boundaries of family expenditure, positioning it as a balanced state between the two extremes of wastefulness (*israf*) and stinginess (*iqtar*). This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *wasatiyyah* (moderation) in financial conduct, ensuring that provision is sufficient for dignity without leading to depletion or hoarding. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining household stability in accordance with divine proportionality.

en.hubeali: And from him, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Amro, from Abdullah Bin Aban who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1<sup>st</sup>, about the spending upon the dependants. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is between the two (limits of) abhorrence – the extravagance and the miserliness’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him (narrator of previous Hadith) from his father from Muhammad ibn ‘Ammar from ‘Abd Allah ibn Aban who has said the following: “Once I asked abu al-Hassan, the 1st, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the expenses of one’s dependents.
He (the Imam) replied, ‘It is between the two detestable limits: namely, excessive spending and severe austerity.’”
